$comment: Roadmap packet C2 — THE parameter-range contract, authored once.
Everything below is generated from this file by `node scripts/gen-node-schema.mjs`:
skald-ui/src/definitions/nodeSchema.generated.ts  (the same tables + a case-by-case lookup mirror)
The editor's stored defaults (node-definitions.ts) read their numbers from the generated
TypeScript, the generated Odin is what the typed setters clamp to and what an exposed-but-
unstored parameter initialises from, and the range-parity gate (RangeParity.test.tsx) asks
the real backend for every editor control. A staleness gate (NodeSchema.test.ts) regenerates
both files in memory and fails when a committed copy differs from this source.
Lookup precedence, implemented in lookup_param_range and mirrored in lookupRange:
1. overrides   (nodeType, name) — consulted before anything else
2. prefixRules  name starts with prefix AND is longer than it (level1, level2, ...)
4. fallback     unknown parameter: wide open, neutral default
A `why` is carried into the generated Odin as a comment. Keep them: they are the reasons
a row has the value it has, and most of them cite a shipped bug.

prefixRules.why: Mixer channel levels: level1, level2, ... Default 1.0 (unity), NOT the wide-open unknown fallback — an exposed channel used to initialize to 0.0 (silently muted) with a ±1e6 clamp.

overrides.name: frequency
overrides.why: A ratio of the played note, not Hz: the generic frequency row gave an exposed FM ratio a [20,20000] Hz setter. Default 2 = the editor's (C2 unified nine defaults; the table said 1).

overrides.name: frequency
overrides.why: An exposed LFO frequency clamped to audio range under the generic row.

overrides.name: amplitude
overrides.why: An LFO's amplitude is a modulation depth in the destination's units, not 0..1.

overrides.name: rate
overrides.why: Wider than the generic rate row's 100 Hz; the card allows 1000.

overrides.name: amplitude
overrides.why: The generic amplitude default is 0.5, but the Noise generator's own fallback and the editor's default are both 1.0 (unity) — so exposing an untouched Noise amplitude used to halve it (SKB-051, closed in 08d5875).

overrides.name: amplitude
overrides.why: SKB-024, THE named case: byte-for-byte the Noise row's shape, held back until C1's backfill existed. The 3->4 save migration stores 0.5 on any exposed-but-unstored Wavetable amplitude (what it generated at), so no existing file changes sound; new nodes store 1.0 and now generate 1.0 when exposed. No shipped example had the case.

overrides.name: amplitude
overrides.why: Same shape as the Wavetable row above, same backfill.

overrides.name: position
overrides.why: The four-shape morph: 0 sine, 1 triangle, 2 saw, 3 square.

overrides.name: decay
overrides.why: C2: the editor's default is 0.2; the shared generic decay row said 0.1 (one of SKB-024's ten divergences). Backfilled 3->4 for exposed-but-unstored.

overrides.name: sustain
overrides.why: C2: editor 0.5, generic row 0.7. Backfilled 3->4.

overrides.name: release
overrides.why: C2: editor 1.0, generic row 0.2. Backfilled 3->4.

overrides.name: attackCurve
overrides.why: E8 (roadmap 9.4 item 2): per-stage curve tension. 0 = linear, the shape every ADSR emitted before this row existed — an exposed-but-untouched attackCurve must generate the same envelope as a patch with no curve at all, so this default is the one number that keeps every pre-E8 patch's goldens byte-identical.

overrides.name: decayCurve
overrides.why: E8, same shape as attackCurve above — 0 = linear.

overrides.name: releaseCurve
overrides.why: E8, same shape as attackCurve above — 0 = linear.

overrides.name: decay
overrides.why: F-A10-17 / C2: the shared decay row's 0 minimum is right for an ADSR stage and wrong for a tail (both editor surfaces say 0.1), and its 0.1 default was a 0.1 s room where the editor means a 3 s hall. Backfilled 3->4.

overrides.name: gain
overrides.why: C2: editor 0.75, generic gain row 1.0. Backfilled 3->4.

overrides.name: outMax
overrides.why: C2: editor 20000 (0..1 -> 0..20000 Hz is the Mapper's canonical job), generic row 1. Bounds stay unbounded. Backfilled 3->4.

overrides.name: tone
overrides.why: The post-shaper one-pole lowpass; the generic table has no tone row.

overrides.name: outputGain
overrides.why: Post-distortion makeup gain (packet B1; F-A06-10). Default 1.0 — bit-identical for every patch that never authored it. Matches the generic gain row's 0..4 span, and the generator clamps to the same bounds at point of use.

overrides.name: amplitude
overrides.why: C5 (F-A02-7): the FM Operator's output level. An exposed-but-untouched operator must stay at the unity it always emitted (the SKB-051 class).

overrides.name: damping
overrides.why: C5 (F-A07-7): 0 = the undamped comb every existing patch has; no generic row carries the name.

generic.name: pulseWidth
generic.why: A8: was {0.0, 1.0}. The oscillator's point-of-use clamp is math.clamp(f32(pw), 0.01, 0.99) and BOTH editor surfaces already say 0.01..0.99 — this row was the only copy claiming 0..1, so an exposed pulseWidth minted a set_pulseWidth advertising a range 2% of which the DSP silently discarded.

generic.name: attack
generic.why: A8: attack/decay/release min was 0.001. Zero is a SUPPORTED value in the engine: the generated envelope branches on `if (attack) > 0 ... else envelope = 1.0` and wraps every stage denominator in math.max(x, 0.000001) so a literal 0 means instant. This row was the only copy forbidding it, so ADSR_set_attack(p, 0) clamped an instant attack up to 1 ms.

generic.name: feedback
generic.why: A8: max was 0.99. The delay's point-of-use clamp is math.clamp(f32(fdbk), 0.0, 0.95) — feedback at or above 1 diverges and NaN-latches the processor. No saved patch ever SOUNDED like 0.99, so this removed a lie, not behaviour.

generic.group: Instrument-level exposure is currently dormant: these values do not produce setters/PARAMS rows. Keep this fallback aligned with the editor/serializer's compile-time polyphony contract.

generic.name: pitchJitter
generic.why: G5 (roadmap 9.18): per-trigger random pitch spread, uniform in ±pitchJitter cents. Default 0 emits no jitter code at all, so an untouched Instrument's output stays byte-identical (KI-018's stealMode sibling — a value read at codegen time, not a runtime-exposed field).

generic.name: velocityJitter
generic.why: G5: per-trigger random velocity spread, uniform in ±velocityJitter, clamped back into [0,1] same as note_on's own velocity clamp. Default 0 emits no jitter code.
